content.text:
Axios now accepts Node 18's built-in `FormData` in the HTTP adapter. It's sent as a normal multipart request instead of failing with "Data after transformation must be a string, an ArrayBuffer, a Buffer, or a Stream".

I checked it against a local server with a `FormData` holding a text field and a `Blob` file named `x.txt`. The body arrived as correct multipart. The `Content-Type` header (including the boundary) and the `Content-Length` header (296) matched the body. Sending a plain `Blob` as the request body also worked.

The adapter test file (`test/unit/adapters/http.js`) gives 89 passing and 5 failing both with and without my change, so the change adds no failures. I didn't look into why those 5 fail.

**What changed:**
- **`lib/utils.js`**: added `isSpecCompliantForm`, which recognises the standard `FormData` (the Node 18+ global and similar ones). I also added a small random-string generator used to make the boundary.
- **`lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js`** (new): turns a standard `FormData` into a multipart stream. It writes each field's headers, handles file values with their filename and content type, and works out `Content-Length` up front. If you already set a boundary in `Content-Type`, it uses yours; otherwise it makes one like `axios-<version>-boundary-<random>`. The header you passed, `multipart/form-data` with no boundary, gets replaced by the full value.
- **`lib/helpers/readBlob.js`** (new): reads the contents of a `Blob` or `File` as a stream.
- **`lib/adapters/http.js`**: checks for standard `FormData` before the existing check for the `form-data` npm package, which still works as before.

One addition beyond the issue: a plain `Blob` used directly as the request body now goes through too. It gets the blob's type (or `application/octet-stream`) as `Content-Type`, plus the right `Content-Length`. I didn't add new tests.
